scenes.text: In one famous photo, all of planet Earth is smaller than a single pixel.
It's called the Pale Blue Dot, taken by Voyager one on February fourteenth, nineteen ninety.
Astronomer Carl Sagan, born on November ninth, pushed NASA to turn the camera back toward home.
The probe was about six billion kilometers away.
From there, Earth filled just twelve percent of one pixel, a tiny speck in a sunbeam.
Everyone who has ever lived is inside that dot.
Does that make your problems feel smaller?

title: All of Earth in less than ONE pixel 🌍
caption: On Feb 14, 1990, Voyager 1 photographed Earth from about 6 billion km away: the Pale Blue Dot, just 0.12 of a pixel. Carl Sagan (born Nov 9, 1934) pushed for the shot. 🌍
